summary: The standalone unified diff named exactly two target files and passed git apply check then apply on a pristine snapshot; the resulting file hashes matched the working patched copy. The JSON-lines bundle parsed as exactly one record with keys for the identifier and the patch text, its embedded diff was byte-identical to the standalone patch, and it applied to a second pristine tree with the same hashes. Replaying the extended 31-case differential on the bundle-patched tree produced zero target deliveries, matching the working patched copy, while the vulnerable copy produced nineteen. A negative-control mutant with only the internal object-form resolution repaired still produced five target deliveries. Bracketed IPv6 was closed logically because no IPv6 address could bind: five spellings stayed on the base IPv6 origin under the patched helper while four changed origin under the vulnerable parser. A sha256 manifest over baseline, working patched, pristine-applied, bundle-applied, patch and bundle files recomputed equal, and a one-byte baseline mutation was detected.
next_hint: Local closure is complete for the exported payload: the bundle reproduces the exact verified tree and behavior, a partial repair is detected, and the manifest is recomputable. The remaining verdict is the external official evaluator run of the bundle; IPv6 wire delivery remains the only unexecuted origin form.
